title: Housing Legislation Amendment (Fair Share for Regional Housing) Bill 2024
short_title: Housing Legislation Amendment (Fair Share for Regional Housing) Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would redirect housing funding toward regional, rural and remote Australia.
It would require Housing Australia and the Housing Australia Future Fund to support local governments and state-owned utilities for building essential infrastructure like sewers and roads.
The minister would have to ensure that at least 30% of Housing Australia's annual funds go to projects outside major cities, and report on compliance yearly.
changes: Adds local councils and government-owned utilities as groups that Housing Australia must assist.
Requires the minister to review how Housing Australia can allocate a minimum 30% of its yearly funding to non-metropolitan projects.
Demands an annual ministerial report to Parliament explaining whether the 30% target was met, and if not, why not.
Forces Housing Australia to detail in its annual report how each type of financial help was spread across states, local areas, utilities, and regional zones.
Adds regional, rural and remote residents as a group whose housing needs the HAFF must address.
Clarifies the HAFF can fund critical enabling infrastructure for social and affordable housing, including affordable rental housing.
summary.affected: Local governments, state-owned utility providers, and people in regional, rural and remote Australia would be affected.
